```{r}
stopifnot(all(rownames(obs) == colnames(atac_by_cl_raw)))
cl_idx_rgnt <- split(seq_len(nrow(obs)), obs$RegionNT)
cl_idx_rg   <- split(seq_len(nrow(obs)), obs$Cluster_Dominant_Region)
cl_idx_nt   <- split(seq_len(nrow(obs)), obs$NT_MSN)
```

```{r}
all_rgnt <- names(cl_idx_rgnt)
```

# "Useable Regions" For GABA/Glut sharing analysis

Regions with both "GABA" and "Glut" clusters.

```{r}
split(sub(".*_", "", all_rgnt), sub("_.*", "", all_rgnt)) %>% 
    lapply(function(x) all(c("Glut", "GABA") %in% x)) %>% 
    .[unlist(.)] %>% 
    names %>% 
    setdiff("Multi") ->
    useable_regions
```

# [RERUN!] Specificity analysis (non-DESeq2)

```{r}
pdir_peak_spec <- file.path(pdir_plots, "RegionalPeaksBySpecificity")
if (!dir.exists(pdir_peak_spec))
    dir.create(pdir_peak_spec)
```


## Specificity calculations

sums are the total sum of the cluster-level CPM values for that peak, so these
values are weighted by balance of clusters (so if there were 3 GABA clusters to
every Glut, GABA peaks would have higher sums). 

this is appropriate because we're only interested in how those total sums are 
partitioned among different groupings of clusters.

first, total sums for each peak:
(only needed if every doing sums not using all the clusters, which as of now
I don't think I'm doing anymore...)

```{r}
peak_sums <- rowSums(atac_by_cl_cpm)
```

utility function: rev-rank (so 1 is the highest)

```{r}
# ranks so that 1 is the highest value:
# > rank(1:5)
# [1] 1 2 3 4 5
# > rev_rank(1:5)
# [1] 5 4 3 2 1
rev_rank <- function(x) {
    rk <- rank(x)
    max(rk) + 1 - rk
}
```

#### IMPORTANT CHECK FOR REVERSE RANKS

Seems more convenient, but I MIGHT GET DIFFERENT PEAKS!

No guarantee that maximizing rank(A)+rank(B) = minimizing rrank(A)+rrank(B) !!

### For Region+NT

next, the sum of those counts found in each RegionNT, and the fraction (the
specificity).

```{r}
# all outputs here are peak-by-RegionNT matrices:

# total sum of normalized counts for each peak in each rgnt
peak_sums_rgnt <- sapply(cl_idx_rgnt, function(i) rowSums(atac_by_cl_cpm[, i, drop=FALSE]))

# fraction of that peak's total found in each rgnt
peak_frac_rgnt <- peak_sums_rgnt / peak_sums

# and the rev_rank of each peak for specificity in each rgnt (1 being most specific)
rrank_peak_frac_rgnt <- apply(peak_frac_rgnt, 2, rev_rank)

# also use regular ranks (which I had used before for finding regional peaks
# shared across NTs) [so 1 is least specific peak]
rank_peak_frac_rgnt <- apply(peak_frac_rgnt, 2, rank)
```

```{r}
## because using all clusters, same as peak_sums
# > max(rowSums(peak_sums_rgnt) - peak_sums)
# [1] 1.455192e-11
```


### For Region

```{r}
peak_sums_rg <- sapply(cl_idx_rg, function(i) rowSums(atac_by_cl_cpm[, i, drop=FALSE]))
peak_frac_rg <- peak_sums_rg / peak_sums
rrank_peak_frac_rg <- apply(peak_frac_rg, 2, rev_rank)
```

### For NT

```{r}
peak_sums_nt <- sapply(cl_idx_nt, function(i) rowSums(atac_by_cl_cpm[, i, drop=FALSE]))
peak_frac_nt <- peak_sums_nt / peak_sums
rrank_peak_frac_nt <- apply(peak_frac_nt, 2, rev_rank)
```


## Summarize specificity metric [ugh]

It is effectively "median specificity of the top 2000 most specific peaks", 
which is the same as saying the specificity of the 1000th most specific peak.

I checked various numbers (like 1e2, 1e3, 1e4) and the relationship is linear
so it doesn't really matter which is used (unless some other calculations are
done using it).

But overall, it's the tendancy for peaks to be found only in that group

### For Region+NT

tabulated into a df for all peaks:

```{r}
rgnt_pk_spec <- left_join(
    reshape2::melt(
        peak_frac_rgnt, 
        varnames = c("peak", "RegionNT"), 
        value.name = "spec"
    ),
    reshape2::melt(
        rrank_peak_frac_rgnt, 
        varnames = c("peak", "RegionNT"), 
        value.name = "rev_rank_spec"
    ),
    by = c("peak", "RegionNT")
)
```

```{r}
    nm_glut <- paste0(rg, "_Glut")
    nm_gaba <- paste0(rg, "_GABA")
    rank_peak_frac_rgnt[, nm_glut] + rank_peak_frac_rgnt[, nm_gaba]
})
```

### Heatmap code (cands_by_region)

cands_by_region is a named list (names are regions), each element a char vector
of peak names.

the essence:

```{r}
# atac_by_cl_cpm %>% 
#     .[unlist(top20_peaks_by_region), ] %>% 
#     t %>% 
#     scale %>% 
#     t %>% 
#     .[, colnames(.) %in% rownames(subset(obs, Cluster_Dominant_Region %in% useable_regions))] ->
#     atac_by_cl_cpm_sub
```


```{r}
make_heatmap <- function(cands_by_region, regions = useable_regions, Z_CLIP=6) {
    
    ## ---------------- config ----------------
    region_levels <- regions                         # enforce this order for rows & cols
    region_pal    <- setNames(brewer.pal(length(region_levels), "Set2"), region_levels)
    
    # preferred NT ordering (others appended afterward)
    nt_preferred  <- c("Glut", "GABA")
    
    # heatmap colors
    hm_cols <- colorRamp2(c(-Z_CLIP, 0, Z_CLIP), c("#38598C", "white", "#B40426"))
    
    ## -------- rows (peaks) from top20 lists, grouped by region ----------
    peaks_concat <- unlist(cands_by_region[region_levels], use.names = FALSE)
    peaks_concat <- peaks_concat[!is.na(peaks_concat)]
    
    peak_region_vec <- unlist(
        lapply(region_levels, function(rg) rep(rg, length(cands_by_region[[rg]]))),
        use.names = FALSE
    )
    peak_region_vec <- peak_region_vec[seq_along(peaks_concat)]
    peak_region_fac <- factor(peak_region_vec, levels = region_levels)
    
    ## ------- columns (clusters), grouped by region, THEN ordered by NT ------
    # keep only clusters in the chosen regions
    obs_sub <- obs %>%
        filter(Cluster_Dominant_Region %in% region_levels)
    
    # NT levels: preferred first (if present), then all remaining NTs
    nt_all     <- as.character(obs_sub$NT_MSN)
    nt_levels  <- c(nt_preferred[nt_preferred %in% nt_all],
                    setdiff(sort(unique(nt_all)), nt_preferred))
    
    # palette for NTs (works for any # of categories)
    nt_pal <- setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(length(nt_levels)), nt_levels)
    
    # enforce factor levels and order columns by Region -> NT -> original order
    ### -> overwrite NT with values derived from NT_MSN
    obs_sub <- obs_sub %>%
        mutate(
            Dominant_Region = factor(as.character(Cluster_Dominant_Region), levels = region_levels),
            NT = factor(as.character(NT_MSN), levels = nt_levels)
        )
    col_order <- rownames(arrange(obs_sub, Dominant_Region, NT))
    col_region_fac <- factor(as.character(obs_sub[col_order, "Dominant_Region", drop = TRUE]),
                             levels = region_levels)
    col_nt_fac     <- factor(as.character(obs_sub[col_order, "NT", drop = TRUE]),
                             levels = nt_levels)
    
    ## -------- matrix subset + z-score per peak (row) ----------
    peaks_present <- intersect(peaks_concat, rownames(atac_by_cl_cpm))
    if (length(peaks_present) == 0) 
        stop("No selected peaks found in matrix.")
    
    keep_idx <- peaks_concat %in% peaks_present
    peaks_concat    <- peaks_concat[keep_idx]
    peak_region_fac <- droplevels(peak_region_fac[keep_idx])
    
    atac_by_cl_cpm_sub <- atac_by_cl_cpm[peaks_concat, col_order, drop = FALSE]
    mat_z <- t(scale(t(atac_by_cl_cpm_sub)))
    mat_z[is.na(mat_z)] <- 0
    mat_z[mat_z >  Z_CLIP] <-  Z_CLIP
    mat_z[mat_z < -Z_CLIP] <- -Z_CLIP
    
    ## -------------- annotations ---------------
    row_anno <- rowAnnotation(
        PeakRegion = peak_region_fac,
        col = list(PeakRegion = region_pal),
        show_annotation_name = TRUE,
        annotation_name_side = "top",
        annotation_legend_param = list(title = "Peak region")
    )
    
    top_anno <- HeatmapAnnotation(
        ClusterRegion = col_region_fac,
        NT            = col_nt_fac,
        col = list(
            ClusterRegion = region_pal,
            NT            = nt_pal
        ),
        show_annotation_name = TRUE,
        annotation_name_side = "left",
        annotation_height = unit(c(3, 3), "mm")  # tweak bar heights if needed
    )
    
    ## -------------- heatmap -------------------
    ht <- Heatmap(
        mat_z,
        name = "z",
        col = hm_cols,
        cluster_rows = FALSE,
        cluster_columns = FALSE,
        show_row_names = FALSE,
        show_column_names = FALSE,
        row_split = peak_region_fac,      # row slice order follows region_levels
        column_split = col_region_fac,    # column slice order follows region_levels
        top_annotation = top_anno,
        left_annotation = row_anno,
        row_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
        column_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
        border = TRUE,
        column_title = "clusters grouped by dominant region & neurotransmitter",
        row_title = "candidate peaks grouped by region"
    )
    return(ht)
}
```
